newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FOCUS-Brazil CVRD sale to fund projects.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Brazil CVRD sale to fund projects.

text.p: Offering a peace pipe to Congressional opponents, Brazil's government has decided that half the proceeds from the sale of mining colossus Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) will finance infrastructure projects.

Planning Minister Antonio Kandir told a Senate committee Thursday 50 percent of the receipts from the sale of its 51 percent stake in CVRD, expected to be Latin America's biggest privatization to date, would pay off public debt.
The rest would be put into a new fund, called the Economic Reconstruction Fund (FRE), which would provide low-cost credit lines for projects aimed principally at infrastructure.
"The political decision has been taken," Kandir told senators on the Infrastructure Committee, adding that the "how" was still under discussion.
The move was a clear concession to Congress, which has been mumbling ominously that it fears CVRD's future private sector owners will not want to fund regional development.
It may also surprise Finance Minister Pedro Malan, who wants the $6.0 billion in CVRD receipts to be used to retire debt.
An aide to Malan said he was unaware a decison had been taken to set up the FRE.

But he said the minister would support the idea so long as the funds were used to finance private sector infrastructure projects and the interest rates charged no less than the costs of raising capital for the National Treasury.
"As the English say, the devil is in the details," the aide said. "There should be no onus on the Treasury."
Earlier this week, officials said bid specifications for the initial block sale of 40-45 percent of CVRD's voting shares, due to take place in April, might be made public on Friday.
But Kandir told reporters before heading into the committee that the government was still in the final phase of preparing the tender details and that they might emerge next Wednesday.

He and National Development Bank (BNDES) head Luiz Carlos Mendonca de Barros confirmed previously announced details of the sale, including guarantees the republic will benefit from potential future mineral discoveries.
Joint venture risk contracts between CVRD and the BNDES would assure the government a 50 percent stake in any as yet unknown "extraordinary" mineral deposit, Kandir said.

Mendonca de Barros also assured senators the government would keep a five-year "golden share" in a holding company known as Valecom that will be established with the initial block sale, and a perpetual "golden share" in the company itself.
A golden share is a right of veto.

Mendonca de Barros reiterated that the sale would take place in three stages -- the block sale, an offer to employees which he said would be worth about 400 million reais, and then domestic and international public offerings.
The CVRD privatization has many foes.
On Wednesday, government-allied senators crushed a renewed left-wing attempt to speed up deliberation of a bill that would make it subject to Congressional approval.
Kandir's avowal on Thursday to use the FRE to continue CVRD's role as a development agent in some of Brazil's poorest parts clearly pleased senators.
The idea would be "restricted to Vale and not extended to other privatizations," the minister said.
((-- Brasilia newsroom 55-61-2230358))
